note: Item wording transcribed verbatim from the study's own CC0 Harvard Dataverse deposit (doi:10.7910/DVN/Y75CP2, 'Jeehp_15_19_raw data.xlsx', the dataset's only file). That sheet is self-documenting: row 1 holds the survey column code (Q15_1..Q15_15), row 2 holds the original IRI item number (IR_Index_1, _3, _5, _6, _7, _8, _12, _13, _15, _16, _21, _22, _23, _25, _26), row 3 the domain, and row 4 the full question text; data start at row 5. mapping_basis=data_labels on that basis. data/dpt_noncognitive_traits.py renames Q15_k -> iri_N using exactly row 2's numbers, so the IRW code carries the instrument's own item numbering rather than presentation order. That rename is the one inferential step the file's labels do not themselves cover, so it was checked against the data: per-item x per-resp frequency profiles reproduce the source column cell for cell in all 74 non-empty cells, 0 mismatches (e.g. iri_1 5/45/76/116/56, iri_12 103/125/40/25/5, iri_8 0/18/40/153/87 -- iri_8 has no resp=1 in either, matching the live resp_min of 2). See verify_dpt_noncog__interpersonal_reactivity.R. Step 3b: all 15 wordings match Davis's canonical IRI numbering (item 1 daydream/fantasize FS, 3 'other guy's point of view' PT-reverse, 22 'pretty soft-hearted person' EC, 26 'reading an interesting story or novel' FS), so the table is the IRI and not another instrument from the same six-scale battery. OPTION ANCHORS ARE NOT FROM THE DEPOSIT: the xlsx stores bare integers with no value labels, so the two endpoint anchors come from the paper's Methods (JEEHP 2018;15:19, PMC6194478, CC BY 4.0), which reads 'The IRI uses a 5-point scale ranging from 4 (describes me very well) to 0 (does not describe me well)'. They are shipped in the paper's own lower case, verbatim. Note the paper describes a 0-4 coding while the deposit and the IRW table store 1-5; Davis's own IRI guide says 'I use a 0 - 4 item response format ... Other researchers often use a 1-5 format instead', so 1 = does not describe me well and 5 = describes me very well. Direction corroborated by content: iri_21 ('two sides to every question') sits at 234/298 in the top two categories while the reverse-worded iri_12 ('becoming extremely involved in a good book or movie is somewhat rare for me') sits at 228/298 in the bottom two. Points 2-4 are unlabelled on the IRI and are left blank rather than padded with their own number. instructions and section_prompt are left blank: the deposit publishes none and the paper reproduces none; the canonical IRI instruction text refers to lettered A-E options that this administration did not use, so it was deliberately not imported. RIGHTS: the source IRW copied from is CC0 (Dataverse) and the paper is CC BY 4.0, and the paper selected only 'non-proprietary' measures. The instrument's rights holder does state a non-commercial restriction -- Davis's 'Guide for Using the Interpersonal Reactivity Index (IRI)', linked as 'Permissions and Advice on Using the IRI' from his official page eckerd.edu/psychology/iri/, says 'The IRI is freely available for all non-commercial uses, and this document may be taken as an explicit granting of permission to use the instrument in such a way. Requests to use the IRI for any commercial project should be directed to davismh@eckerd.edu.' That is an NC clause with no redistribution bar and no fee, i.e. the same shape as the ECR-R case, so under itemtext_standard.md the open source licence governs and the wording ships -- with wording_rights=NC recorded on every row and a public issues-page entry. Checked and NOT applicable: no clause barring reproduction or distribution (contrast WHOQOL), and no licence fee (contrast TAS-20).
public_note: Item wording for this table is the Interpersonal Reactivity Index, whose author grants use 'for all non-commercial uses' only, so every row carries wording_rights=NC; the response anchors come from the study's paper (1 = does not describe me well, 5 = describes me very well) and only those two scale points are labelled on the IRI, so options 2-4 are deliberately blank.
